references.text: God's promise that Sarah would bear a son, despite her old age.
The fulfillment of God's promise to Abraham that Sarah would bear a son, whom they named Isaac.
God confirms that the covenant will be established with Isaac, whom Sarah will bear next year.
Paul explains that it is through Isaac that Abraham's offspring will be reckoned, quoting the promise that Sarah will have a son.
Paul refers to Isaac as the child of promise, illustrating the difference between those born according to the flesh and those born through the promise.
Sarah herself received power to conceive, even past her age, because she believed that He who had promised was faithful.
Confirmation that Isaac is the sole heir in the eternal covenant established in 17:19.
Direct quote/allusion to the prophecy about Sarah's son as the basis for the doctrine of God's election.
Fulfillment of God's command to name the son Isaac.
Contrast between Ishmael and Isaac showing that only Isaac is the heir in the eternal covenant.
The same prophecy given by an angel, emphasizing God's power to fulfill the promise.
Historical fulfillment of the prophecy about Sarah giving birth at the appointed time.
Sarah's confirmation that the miracle (birth in old age) has been fulfilled as promised.
The same prophetic revelation given by an angel, confirming the promise of a son.
Typological parallel: A miraculous birth prophecy to a barren woman (Mary) fulfilled in Jesus.
Same context: God's command to keep the covenant linked to Isaac.
Typological parallel: Angelic prophecy of a miraculous birth fulfilled in Jesus.
Definition of the eternal covenant, which is then specified for Isaac in Gen 17:19.
Confirmation that the covenant regarding the land and descendants is transferred to Isaac's son, Jacob.
Direct reference to the covenant of blessing for all nations, which is linked to Isaac.
Direct quote of the prophecy that the lineage will continue through Isaac.
Confirmation that God is Isaac's God and that the promise of the land is transferred to his descendant.
Same context: God's promise that Abraham will become the father of many nations, which will be carried forward through Isaac.
